text.p: Following are some of the major events to have occurred on March 7 in history:
1765 - Joseph-Nicephore Niepce, French chemist and pioneer in photography, born. He is said to have produced a photograph on metal, the world's first.
1785 - Alessandro Manzoni, Italian author of "The Betrothed", regarded by some as the most notable novel in Italian literature, born.
1793 - France declared war on Spain during the French Revolution.
1802 - Sir Edwin Henry Landseer, English animal painter and sculptor, born. Sculptor of the lions in London's Trafalgar Square.

1809 - Jean-Pierre-Francois Blanchard, French balloonist, died. With John Jeffries he was the first man to cross the English channel by balloon. Also inventor of the parachute, he died in Paris shortly after falling from his balloon at The Hague.
1838 - Famous operatic soprano Jenny Lind, known as the "Swedish Nightingale", made her debut.
1850 - Tomas Garrigue Masaryk, patriot, scholar and poet who later became first president of Czechoslovakia, born.
1875 - Maurice Ravel, French composer best known for his ballets "Bolero" and "Daphnis and Chloe", born.
1876 - Alexander Graham Bell received a patent for his invention of the telephone.
1917 - The world's first jazz record, "The Dixie Jazz Band One Step", recorded by Nick LaRocca's Original Dixieland Jazz Band, was released by RCA Victor in Camden, N.J.
1918 - The Bolsheviks changed their name to the Russian Communist Party.
1932 - French Prime Minister Aristide Briand, who won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1926, died. He pioneered the idea of a United States of Europe.
1936 - Germany violated the Treaty of Versailles and the Locarno Pact by re-occupying the demilitarised zone of Rhineland.
1945 - The U.S. 9th Armoured Division captured the key bridge over the Rhine at Remagen, Germany, which helped shorten the Second World War.
1951 - Iranian Prime Minister Ali Razmara was assassinated by a religious fanatic in a mosque in Tehran.
1965 - West German Chancellor Ludwig Erhard said West Germany would seek to establish diplomatic relations with Israel.
1973 - The government of Sheikh Mujibur Rahman won a landslide victory in Bangladesh's first general election.
1978 - 38 black nationalists were killed during a Rhodesian raid on a guerrilla base in Zambia.
1978 - Burmese President Ne Win was re-elected for a second term.
1983 - 96 miners were killed in a gas explosion at a coal mine near Eregli, Turkey.
1989 - Iran broke off diplomatic relations with Britain over Salman Rushdie's novel Satanic Verses.
1992 - Former Soviet foreign minister Eduard Shevardnadze returned to his native Georgia to help end the chaos in that country.
1992 - A new four-party coalition government, led by Jean-Luc Dehaene, was formed in Belgium.
1993 - Afghanistan's rival leaders signed a peace accord to end months of bloody fighting in Kabul that had killed thousands of civilians.
1994 - Poland said it would join Hungary in applying for membership of the European Union.
1994 - ANC chief Nelson Mandela rejected a demand by white right-wingers for a separate homeland in South Africa, saying it would never happen in his lifetime.
1996 - Three U.S. servicemen were jailed in Japan for up to seven years for the abduction and rape of an Okinawa schoolgirl in 1995.
